sketch0.title: Combine requirements with AND and OR

sc_and_all_conditions.title: What AND means
sc_and_all_conditions.prompt: In a `WHERE` clause, what does `AND` do?
sc_and_all_conditions.hint: A row must pass more than one test when `AND` is used.

help.concept: `AND` combines conditions so only rows that make every combined condition true are returned.
help.hint_1: Think about whether one true condition is enough, or whether all listed conditions must be true.
help.hint_2: Compare `AND` with a checklist: if one item fails, the row is filtered out.

options.a: It returns rows if at least one condition is true.
options.b: It returns rows only if all conditions are true.
options.c: It sorts rows from smallest to largest.
options.d: It selects every column in the table.

fb_and_keyword.title: Complete the filter keyword
fb_and_keyword.prompt: Fill in the missing SQL keyword.
fb_and_keyword.hint: Use the keyword that requires both conditions to be true.

help.concept: SQL has a logical operator for cases where every connected condition must be true.
help.hint_1: This is not the keyword for either/or logic.
help.hint_2: The missing word joins two conditions into one stricter filter.

fb_and_keyword.template: SELECT name FROM products WHERE category = 'Art' [blank1] price < 20;

sc_parentheses_clarity.title: Parentheses make mixed logic clearer
sc_parentheses_clarity.prompt: Why is `WHERE (category = 'Art' OR category = 'Stationery') AND stock > 20` safer to read than leaving out the parentheses?
sc_parentheses_clarity.hint: Look for the answer about grouping the category conditions before checking stock.

help.concept: Parentheses group conditions so the intended logic is explicit when `AND` and `OR` appear together.
help.hint_1: The grouped part decides which category test belongs together as one unit.
help.hint_2: The safer version makes SQL check the two category options together, then apply the stock rule.

options.a: It groups the OR conditions so the stock rule applies to the whole category group.
options.b: It automatically sorts the results by stock.
options.c: It changes text values into numbers before filtering.
options.d: It removes duplicate rows from the table.

mc_and_vs_or.title: Choose filters that require both conditions
mc_and_vs_or.prompt: Which WHERE clauses return only products that are in the Home category and have stock less than 10? Choose all that apply.
mc_and_vs_or.hint: You need both category and stock rules to be true for the same row.

help.concept: When a query must satisfy two conditions at once, use AND so both tests apply to each row.
help.hint_1: One condition should check `category`, and the other should check `stock < 10`.
help.hint_2: Reject any option that uses OR or that changes the stock comparison away from 'less than 10'.

try-and_conditions-sketch1.title: Require Category and Stock Together
try-and_conditions-sketch1.prompt: Prepare a bulk-order list. Return `name`, `category`, and `stock` from `products`, in that order. Keep only `Stationery` products with stock of at least `15`.
try-and_conditions-sketch1.hint: Write one category condition and one stock condition, then connect them with AND.

help.concept: AND keeps a row only when every connected condition is true.
help.hint_1: Write one category condition and one stock condition, then connect them with AND.
help.hint_2: Run the query and compare the returned rows and columns with the requirement.

try-and_conditions-sketch1.starterCode:
-- Require both the category and stock rules.
SELECT name, category, stock
FROM products
WHERE category = 'Stationery'
try-and_conditions-sketch1.solutionCode:
SELECT name, category, stock
FROM products
WHERE category = 'Stationery'
  AND stock >= 15;

sourceChecks.message: Use the `products` table in the FROM clause.
Select the required columns in the requested order: `name`, `category`, `stock`.

practice-grouped-conditions.title: Practice: Group mixed conditions safely
practice-grouped-conditions.prompt: Return `name`, `category`, and `price` from `products`, in that order. Keep `Home` or `Art` products, and require every kept product to cost at most `30`.
practice-grouped-conditions.hint: Group the two category alternatives in parentheses, then connect the price condition with AND.

help.concept: Parentheses keep an OR group together so a following AND rule applies to every alternative.
help.hint_1: Group the two category alternatives in parentheses, then connect the price condition with AND.
help.hint_2: Run the query and compare the returned rows and columns with the requirement.

practice-grouped-conditions.starterCode:
-- Group the two acceptable categories before applying the price rule.
SELECT name, category, price
FROM products
WHERE
practice-grouped-conditions.solutionCode:
SELECT name, category, price
FROM products
WHERE (category = 'Home' OR category = 'Art')
  AND price <= 30;

practice-debug-filter.prompt: The starter query contains an invalid comparison operator. Repair it so the result returns `name` and `price` from `products` for items priced at least `20`.
practice-debug-filter.hint: SQL writes “greater than or equal to” with the two characters in the opposite order from the broken starter.

and_all_rules.title: Combine requirements with AND and OR
and_all_rules.bodyMarkdown:
Use logical operators when one condition is not enough:

- `AND` means every connected condition must be true.
- `OR` means any connected alternative may be true.

Translate the requirement before choosing the operator: **all of these** usually means AND; **any of these** usually means OR.

or_alternatives.title: Group and debug mixed conditions
or_alternatives.bodyMarkdown:
When AND and OR appear together, use parentheses to make the intended grouping explicit.

When a filter is wrong, compare the query with the requirement one condition at a time: operator, literal, logical connector, grouping, then clause order.
